name: pdk-iceberg-loader-schema
instr:
Our daily order exports are Arrow IPC streams that we load into Iceberg with `load_ipc_stream_to_iceberg(path, ('shop', 'orders'), catalog, LoaderConfig(write_mode='append', schema_evolution=True))`. The shop backend moved to a new exporter on 5 October, and since then some loads fail and others store numbers that aren't what was exported. Exports from before and after the switch are in /data/exports/.

With schema_evolution on, every value of every export, old or new, should read back from the table exactly as exported, and a value an export doesn't have should read back as NULL. A column whose type arrives wider in a way Iceberg allows (int to long, float to double, more decimal digits at the same scale) should be widened in place, keeping the rows already there, and loading an older export afterwards must not narrow it again. Loading the exports file by file, or all their batches in one `load_batches_to_iceberg` call with any `commit_interval`, should give the same table.

When a column keeps its type (schema_evolution off, or a change Iceberg can't make), a value the column can't hold exactly, such as a whole number out of range, a fraction for a whole number column, a decimal with too many digits or text that isn't a number, should be stored as NULL while the other values still load. Floats are still rounded to the column's precision.
